title: Chemotherapy: how a course goes
what: Medicines against a tumor are given into a vein through a drip. The course runs in cycles: treatment days and rest days.
why: For cancer, as decided by your oncologist.
duration: one infusion takes from 30 minutes to several hours; a course lasts several weeks or months
tell_doctor: All medicines, vitamins, and herbs, since some cannot be combined with chemo
A fever, cough, or infection in recent days
How you handled the last cycle: nausea, weakness, numbness

prepare.title: Tests
prepare.text: Before each cycle, a blood test is usually taken. If it is poor, the cycle may be postponed.

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: Usually a light breakfast is fine in the morning. Check with the clinic.

prepare.title: Medicines
prepare.text: Do not stop or add anything on your own. Take anti-nausea medicines on your doctor's schedule.

prepare.title: Time
prepare.text: The infusion can be long, so bring water, a snack, and a book.

bring: Water, a snack, a blanket, headphones
steps: The nurse checks your tests and how you feel
A line is placed in a vein, or connected to a port
First you get anti-nausea and anti-allergy medicines
Then the chemotherapy drip is connected
The nurse watches how you feel
At the end, the line is flushed and disconnected
feel: The drip itself usually does not hurt
You may have nausea, weakness, or a change in taste, different on different days
If it burns at the injection site, tell the nurse right away
after: Drink enough water, unless your doctor limited it
Wash your hands and avoid contact with sick people
Keep notes on how you feel and show your doctor
Take medicines for side effects on schedule
red_flags: A fever of 38°C (100.4°F) or higher: call your doctor or emergency services right away
Shortness of breath, a rash, or a swollen face during or after the drip: call emergency services
Vomiting so you cannot drink, or severe diarrhea
Bleeding or bruises for no reason

faq.a: Not with every medicine. Your doctor will tell you what to expect with your plan.
Many people do. It depends on the plan and how you feel, so talk to your doctor.

faq.q: Why is a fever so dangerous?
faq.a: Chemo lowers your defense against infection. Even a slight fever needs a quick call to your doctor.

reminders.text: Chemotherapy infusion tomorrow. Have your tests done if needed. Bring water, a snack, and a blanket.
